info.title: Cryptificate local service
info.summary: Submit designs and circuits for Lean-checked analysis, run experiments, poll jobs and download evidence bundles.
info.description:
HTTP API of `cryptificate serve`, the local Cryptificate service. The web workbench and the Python client (`python/cryptificate`) use it; the `cryptificate check` and `experiment` commands run the same pipelines in-process instead.

**Scope.** This document describes every route the service answers. Request and report bodies are described by the JSON Schemas in `schemas/` (referenced here with `$ref`); the served copy at `GET /api/openapi.json` embeds them under `components/schemas`. Examples are responses recorded from a live service (release engine, Lean checker), except the 500 example, which shows the fixed body of that response. They were recorded on the release branch before its version was set to 0.2.0, so their version fields read 0.1.0. Field elements are strings: two hex digits for GF(2^8), canonical decimals below the modulus for BN254.

**Security model.** The service is a single-user local tool and has no authentication. It binds to 127.0.0.1 by default; `--host` can bind elsewhere, and then anyone who can reach the address can run jobs. Every request must carry a `Host` header naming a loopback address (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`) or the bound host, which rejects DNS-rebinding pages. State-changing requests (every method other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS) are accepted only same-origin: when an `Origin` header is present it must be `http://<allowed host>:<port>` of this service or one of the origins given with `--allow-origin` / `CRYPTIFICATE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`; without `Origin`, a `Sec-Fetch-Site` header other than `same-origin` or `none` is rejected. Clients outside a browser (curl, Python) send neither header and are accepted. A rejected request gets 403 `forbidden`. There are no CORS headers: cross-origin browser reads are not supported. Every response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`.

**Limits.** JSON bodies are at most 256 KiB (413 beyond, and the connection is closed). One job runs at a time and at most two wait behind it (`limits.maxQueued` in the capabilities); a further submission gets 429 with `Retry-After: 30`. There is no per-client rate limit beyond this queue. Each job runs under a time budget (`limits.analysisBudgetSeconds`, or the experiment profile's `budget.totalSeconds`), and each Lean run under `limits.leanTimeoutSeconds`.

**Job lifecycle.** `POST /api/analyses` or `POST /api/experiments` answers 202 with a job summary and a `Location` header. The job moves `queued` -> `running` -> one of `completed`, `failed`, `timeout`, `cancelled` or `invalid` (terminal). Poll `GET /api/jobs/{id}`: while it runs, `steps` and a partial `report` are visible. When the state is terminal and `bundle` is true, `GET /api/jobs/{id}/bundle` returns the evidence bundle. Finished jobs survive a restart of the service (the 200 most recently updated are loaded at start). Jobs that were queued or running when the service stopped are not resumed: they read `cancelled`, or `failed` with error code `interrupted`. There is no endpoint that lists jobs; keep the ids you submit.

**Errors.** Every error is JSON with a stable `error.code` (see `ErrorResponse`). A request under `/api/` that matches no operation described here (an unknown path, or a described path with a method it does not list) answers 404 `not-found` when its method is GET or POST, and 405 `method-not-allowed` for any other method, HEAD and OPTIONS included. No response sends an `Allow` header. An unexpected failure answers 500 `internal`.

**Stability.** Paths, status codes, error codes and the members described in the schemas are the supported surface. New optional members may be added to responses; clients should ignore members they do not know. Requests are checked strictly: unknown members are rejected.

get.summary: Models, profiles, limits and toolchain availability
get.description: Reports what this installation can do: the supported design models, the experiment profiles and their budgets, the request and queue limits, and whether the Lean toolchain, rustc and the engine are available. Cheap; the workbench polls it every 15 s.
The OpenAPI 3.1 description of this API, self-contained: the JSON Schemas from `schemas/` are embedded under `components/schemas` and every `$ref` is local.

missing.summary: Service started from a checkout without the description

post.description: Checks a candidate design, and optionally a linear circuit against one of its matrices. The body is shape-checked before a job is created (400 on any problem, with every issue listed); the engine then validates it in depth as the job's first step, so a request that passes the shape check can still end in state `invalid`.

wrong-wire.summary: AES design with a mis-wired MixColumns circuit

post.description: Searches for cheaper circuits for the design's matrix, checks each shortlisted candidate's equivalence in Lean, tests the generated Rust and times it against baselines under the chosen profile's budget. Same submission rules as analyses.

quick.summary: Quick profile with a fixed seed

get.description: Current state, progress steps, queue position (while queued), error (when one occurred) and the report, which is partial while the job runs and final once the state is terminal. Poll until `state` is one of completed, failed, timeout, cancelled or invalid; the workbench polls every 800 ms, and once a second is plenty for scripts.

claims.title: Matrix is MDS (branch number 5)
claims.note: Lean checked CryptificateJob.matrix_mds using only the standard axioms.

claims.title: Row offsets are pairwise distinct
claims.note: Lean checked CryptificateJob.offsets_optimal using only the standard axioms.

claims.title: S-box is a permutation
claims.note: Lean checked CryptificateJob.sbox_bijective using only the standard axioms.

claims.title: At least 25 active S-boxes over 4 rounds

evidence.label: Lean-checked proof
evidence.type: ∀ (sbox : GF256 → GF256), Function.Injective sbox → ∀ (keys : ℕ → Fin 16 → GF256) (x y : Fin 16 → GF256), x ≠ y → (CryptificateJob.candRounds / 4 * 25 + if 2 ≤ CryptificateJob.candRounds % 4 then 5 else 0) ≤ Cryptificate.activeSboxes CryptificateJob.candMatrix CryptificateJob.candOffsets sbox keys x y CryptificateJob.candRounds

claims.note: Lean checked CryptificateJob.activity_bound using only the standard axioms.

claims.title: Differential uniformity of the S-box table is 4
claims.note: Lean checked CryptificateJob.sbox_differential using only the standard axioms. For no nonzero input difference a and output difference b (b may be 00) do more than 4 of the 256 inputs x satisfy S(x ⊕ a) ⊕ S(x) = b; input difference 01 gives output difference 1F for exactly 4. This is a property of the table alone, not a bound on any trail or differential of the cipher.

claims.title: Linearity of the S-box table is 32
claims.note: Lean checked CryptificateJob.sbox_linearity using only the standard axioms. No Walsh coefficient at a nonzero output mask exceeds 32 in absolute value (nonlinearity 112); the one at input mask 01 and output mask 48 reaches it. This is a property of the table alone, not a bound on any linear trail or hull of the cipher.

evidence.label: Lean-checked counterexample
evidence.type: CryptificateJob.candProgram.WellFormed ∧ CryptificateJob.candMatrix.mulVec CryptificateJob.witnessInput = CryptificateJob.witnessExpected ∧ CryptificateJob.candProgram.eval CryptificateJob.witnessInput = CryptificateJob.witnessActual ∧ ¬∀ (x : Fin 4 → GF256), CryptificateJob.candProgram.eval x = CryptificateJob.candMatrix.mulVec x

post.description: A queued job is removed from the queue and becomes `cancelled` at once. A running job is signalled (its whole process group is killed) and becomes `cancelled` shortly after; completed checkpoints and the partial report are kept. Stopping a finished job changes nothing. The request body is ignored and no Content-Type is required. The response is the summary at the time of the call, so a running job may still read `running`: poll to see the final state.

200.description: The job summary after the stop request.

get.description: A deterministic gzip-compressed tar archive with the normalized inputs, the report, the generated Lean certificates and the checker output, the toolchain pins, native sources and measurements when those steps ran, and VERIFY.md. Available when the job is terminal, not `invalid`, and has a report (`bundle: true` in the job). The same job always yields the same bytes. `cryptificate verify <bundle>` re-checks it.

409.description: There is no bundle: the job is still queued or running, ended before producing a report, or its request was invalid.

no-report.summary: The job was stopped before it produced a report

error.message: the job ended before it produced a report

get.description: The self-contained HTML evidence report of the job: byte for byte the `report.html` of its evidence bundle, rendered from the bundled (path-scrubbed) report and toolchain pins. Inline CSS, no scripts and no external requests; the response carries the same Content Security Policy the page declares. Available under the same conditions as the bundle. The page is a rendering of `report.json`, not evidence: `cryptificate verify` re-checks the bundle and never reads `report.html`.

Content-Security-Policy.description: default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'

409.description: There is no report to render: the job is still queued or running, ended before producing a report, or its request was invalid.

no-report.summary: The job was stopped before it produced a report

error.message: the job ended before it produced a report

get.description: Serves the built workbench from apps/web/dist when it exists: static files, with index.html for any other path without a file extension (client-side routes). Without a built UI, `/` returns a short page that points to the API. HEAD is answered like GET; other methods on non-API paths answer 405. Not part of the JSON API.

JobId.name: id
JobId.description: Job id as returned at submission: 32 lowercase hex digits. Any other value is answered with 404.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before submitting again (always 30).

Connection.description: close: the service stops reading the oversized body.

Accepted.description: The job was created and queued. Poll the job at the `Location` path.

BadRequest.description: The body is not JSON (`bad-json`) or not a request of the documented shape (`invalid-request`, with every issue in `errors`, at most 50).

error.message: request body is not valid JSON

invalid-request.summary: A number where a field element string belongs, and too few rounds

error.message: /design/matrix/0/1: field elements are strings, not numbers

errors.message: field elements are strings, not numbers

TooLarge.description: The body exceeds 256 KiB (`body-too-large`). The connection is closed; a client still uploading may see the connection reset instead of this response.

QueueFull.description: One job is running and two are queued (`queue-full`). Retry after the indicated delay.

error.message: one job is running and the queue is full; try again later

NoSuchJob.description: No job has this id (`not-found`). Ids are random. After a restart the service loads the 200 most recently updated jobs from its state directory; older ids answer 404.

Forbidden.description: The request failed the Host/Origin policy (see the security model above).

host.summary: Host header is not a loopback address

error.message: Host header is not a loopback address

Internal.description: An unexpected failure in the service (`internal`). Job failures are not reported this way: they are a job in state `failed` with an `error`.
